name: RBF axion search
summary: One of the earliest Galactic-halo microwave-cavity axion searches, jointly conducted by Rochester, Brookhaven and Fermilab.
detection_principle: A strong field converts nonrelativistic axions to narrowband photons in a tunable microwave cavity, with power spectra tested for excesses.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 1989 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Results of a laboratory search for cosmic axions and other weakly coupled light particles

collaboration.name: RBF axion search Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Upper limits on axion coupling and abundance were obtained; sensitivity remains above benchmark invisible-axion predictions.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
